c.tagline: The Friendly City — Algoa Bay beaches and gateway to Addo's elephants.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis must be booked by phone or app rather than hailed in the street; Uber and Bolt are the usual choice, while shared minibus taxis run fixed routes cheaply for locals.

emergency.note: From a mobile phone 112 connects to all emergency services; 10111 is the police and 10177 is the ambulance service.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Richmond Hill: Stanley Street, Richmond Hill, Port Elizabeth

avoid.reason: Caution in the CBD and townships; muggings at night

hood_desc: The prime seaside base along Marine Drive, with Hobie and Pollok beaches, Nelson Mandela University, the Boardwalk casino-and-dining complex and most of the city's beachfront hotels.
A beachfront neighbourhood centred on Kings Beach and the promenade, with the harbour close by; a classic, relaxed seaside stay a short hop from the centre.
The historic British-colonial core around the Donkin Reserve, the Campanile bell tower and the Route 67 public-art trail; rich in heritage but quiet after business hours.
A revived hilltop district above the centre, best known for the Stanley Street strip of trendy restaurants, cafés and bars — the city's go-to for eating out and nightlife.
A leafy, affluent inland suburb of large homes and guesthouses next to the airport, offering a quiet, green base a short drive from both the beaches and the centre.
lodging: Protea Hotel by Marriott Port Elizabeth Marine

water.note: Tap water is treated and generally safe, though drought restrictions can affect supply.

transit.hours: Algoa buses run mainly on weekday commuter schedules (roughly 6 AM to 6 PM) with very limited evening and weekend service; informal minibus taxis run longer hours.
transit.pay: Algoa buses take cash and rechargeable fare cards; minibus taxis are cash-only, paid to the driver at fixed route fares.
transit.note: Public transport is limited and the city is car-dependent. The Algoa Bus Company runs scheduled routes from Market Square, supplemented by informal minibus taxis; a planned bus-rapid-transit system remains largely unfinished, so most visitors use Uber/Bolt or rent a car.

bus: Intercity coaches (Intercape and others) & minibus taxis

transit.m: Metered taxi to the city centre (10-15 min)

tip.r: ~10-15% at restaurants and for guides; tip petrol attendants and informal car guards a few rand.
